prize_parts.citation: for discoveries of the physiology and active form of glucagon-like peptide-1 that enabled incretin-based treatment of type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: Round 1 produced one configuration from six members, but I do not rely on the count. B041 stands on the discovery chain. Holst established the incretin effect and GLP-1 secretion in humans. Drucker defined proglucagon processing and the actions of its peptides. Mojsov identified the truncated bioactive peptide, which is the step that turned a hormone into a druggable target. Independent randomized outcome trials in diabetes, obesity, and cardiovascular and renal disease have since validated the mechanism, and the work is decades old, so recognition is neither premature nor late. The citation I propose honours the physiology and the active peptide form. It says nothing of the analogue programme, which keeps the prize anchored to discovery without naming a fourth person.
statement.case_against: Attribution remains the weakness and round 1 did not remove it. Habener and other early contributors are outside the credited names. Priority for the active peptide is contested, and no member can adjudicate it from the permitted files. Knudsen led the acylated long-acting agonists that reached patients, and the three-person cap excludes her. If the committee decides the prize must reward the therapy and not the physiology, my trio is wrong in one name. I also concede that a single-part prize leaves out every other shortlisted achievement, and that long-term safety data on chronic incretin therapy are still accumulating, although that does not touch the core discovery.

responses.point: Sandberg now accepts the Drucker, Holst and Mojsov trio but still calls Knudsen's acylated analogue programme a distinct achievement and not a later detail, and he points to prize history in which new chemistry that made a mechanism into a therapy was credited.
responses.response: I accept that Knudsen's step was distinct and decisive for patients, and I withdraw any suggestion that it is a mere detail. My point is narrower. The question for this ballot is which step the discovery criterion rewards, and the identification of the active peptide is what defined the target that her chemistry then optimized. Your point about precedent is fair, but those cases usually involved chemistry that created the mechanism or the class, whereas here the mechanism existed before the analogues. My position would change only if the priority record showed that Mojsov's claim to the active peptide is materially weaker than I assume. Absent that, I keep the trio and I do not read your Knudsen point as requiring a swap.

responses.point: Perlmann agreed with excluding Rosenberg from CAR-T, disagreed that B023 should rank as low as eighth because multiple approved products and a decade of durable remissions are not early and the checkpoint prize concerned a different mechanism, and kept B023 as an alternative and not a lead because of Eshhar's missing credit.
responses.response: You have moved me. My earliness concern after the checkpoint prize was weak, since approved CAR-T products and durable remissions in refractory disease are established and the mechanism is distinct from checkpoint blockade. I now treat B023 as the most credible next candidate and I have changed its place in my alternatives to first. I still agree with you that Eshhar's chimeric receptor concept is a real attribution gap that the credited names cannot close. I also keep June and Sadelain without Rosenberg, because adoptive cell transfer with tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes is a separate lineage from receptor engineering. Those two points are why B023 stays an alternative and not a lead for me.

responses.point: Linnarsson ranks CAR-T second because a new modality with durable remissions in refractory leukaemia and lymphoma is the demonstrated human benefit this prize rewards, and he says the Eshhar problem bears on which names are credited and not on its rank.
responses.response: I agree that the Eshhar problem should affect the choice of names and not the ranking, and that is where the real difficulty lies. Eshhar and Gross are outside the credited list, so a June and Sadelain pair may be defensible as the engineered, clinically validated step, but a citation would have to be worded narrowly. I do not yet know whether that wording can be written without understating the chimeric receptor concept. That is why I cannot support B023 as part of a shared prize this year. On your fixed-trio question, I agree with you against adding a fourth name to B041, and your earlier idea of swapping Knudsen for Mojsov is one I reject for the reasons I gave to Sandberg.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius lists B044 (TNF blockade) as her first alternative and says the contested priority record means the committee may reasonably decide the B041 credit is too contentious to resolve fairly.
responses.response: I take the possibility seriously, but I do not think contested priority justifies setting B041 aside. The three people I name each have a documented, independently verifiable step, and an incomplete trio is a limitation of the three-person rule that applies to nearly every strong candidate here. Holding back the strongest case on the list because one name is disputed would penalise the science for a problem of attribution. On B044, I recognise the clean Feldmann and Maini attribution, but my position from round 1 stands. Its principle of single-target cytokine therapy is already well recognised, and a B041 plus B044 configuration would need four or five names against the three-person limit. I have not added it to my alternatives.

responses.point: El-Manira ranked optogenetics second and said the credit question for any three-person configuration there is unresolved, and she described the credit problem in B041 as not solved by the opening trios.
responses.response: Your caution that the opening trios did not solve the credit problem is right, and I made it the centre of my case against. Where I differ is on remedy. I would not pair B041 with a second part, because B014 has at least three separate contributions and six credited names, so any cut would leave out strong claimants, and my round-1 response on this stands. A single B041 part with a narrowly worded citation limits the exposure to one contested name, while a two-part prize would add several. I take your point on long-term safety of chronic incretin therapy as a caveat and not a barrier.

uncertainties: Priority for identification of the active GLP-1 peptide, including the position of Habener and others outside the credited names, cannot be verified from the permitted files and is the main factor that could change my third name.

Whether Knudsen should replace Mojsov depends on whether the committee weights peptide identification or drug development more heavily, and I have not found a case for the swap that I find stronger than the discovery argument.
Whether a narrowly worded B023 pair of June and Sadelain could be defended given Eshhar and Gross are outside the credited names.
Long-term safety of chronic incretin therapy is still accumulating.
statement.conflict_note: No conflict requires recusal. My documented connections are a postdoc with Paul Greengard and about twenty co-authored works with Thomas Perlmann. Neither involves a credited name on any shortlisted ballot, and I infer no further ties from shared topics or institutions. I do not claim any private information about the nominations.
